newsitem.title: GERMANY: German analysts try to deflect insider spotlight.
newsitem.headline: German analysts try to deflect insider spotlight.

text.p: The German analysts' and investment advisers' association DVFA on Monday attacked proposals to classify analysts as "primary insiders" in a forthcoming banking law.

Germany's BAWe Federal Securities Trading Authority, in charge of implementing the country's fledgling ban on insider trading, has said analysts are privy to enough classified information to make them primary insiders.
The term currently applies largely to employees of companies who can be prosecuted for passing on or acting upon market-moving information before it is publicly announced.

DVFA managing director Ulrike Diehl told a press conference on Monday that such a classification was ludicrous for analysts and plans to introduce it were an "acute attack" on the competitiveness of the German capital markets.
Germany must not have regulations that do not apply elsewhere, Diehl warned, or it will run the risk that international firms will close down their German research departments.
She said analysts fulfilled a key function in collecting and passing on information to investors.
